reference: GNU coreutils mv from the isolated runner PATH; the metadata contract is grounded in Bash type/help builtins and the mv documentation in the source.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and help metadata
Quoted relative paths and binary file contents
Force overwrite, no-clobber, and interactive EOF behavior
Additional bounded regular-file, hardlink, symlink and multi-operand error continuation regressions.
GNU long options, abbreviations and diagnostics, -b/--backup/-S, -u/--update, --exchange, and FIFOs and backups moved across file systems (the private /tmp tmpfs) (guest pass 5, G74/G76/G78).

Clean-room pass (agent 4): numbered/existing backups and suffix rules, --backup/$VERSION_CONTROL diagnostics and conflicts, -f/-i/-n/--update precedence, prompt and just-created ordering, directory and same-file errors, cross-device trees (FIFO, symlink, hard links, set-group-ID mode), cross-device failures with unbackup, --exchange and trailing-slash rules.
exclusions: EXDEV copy-and-remove fallback is deferred because the fixture runner exposes only one writable filesystem tree; exercising it needs a disposable environment with two distinct writable filesystems or a reviewed EXDEV syscall mock.
Interactive tests use EOF and bounded here-strings; real PTY behavior is not qualified.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports mv as a builtin and exposes its documented synopsis and no-clobber help text.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t mv) == builtin ]] || exit 1
h=$(help mv) || exit 1
[[ $h == *"SRC... DST"* && $h == *"-n   no-clobber: never overwrite"* ]] || exit 1
printf 'builtin help contract
'

cases.purpose: Move a relative file with spaces and embedded NUL bytes using --; GNU mv is the independent behavior oracle and the tree comparison checks exact bytes and source removal.
cases.script:
printf 'left\000right\n' > 'source file'
mv -- 'source file' 'renamed file'

cases.purpose: Move multiple relative sources into a directory with -t, including an operand beginning with a dash after --; GNU mv supplies status and filesystem expectations.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf 'alpha\n' > alpha
printf 'dash\n' > -beta
mv -t destination -- alpha -beta

cases.purpose: Check -f replaces an existing regular destination with source bytes and removes the source; GNU mv is the independent oracle.
cases.script:
printf 'new contents\n' > source
printf 'old contents\n' > destination
mv -f source destination

cases.purpose: Check -n leaves an existing destination untouched and retains the skipped source; GNU mv determines the reference exit status.
cases.script:
printf 'source bytes\n' > source
printf 'destination bytes\n' > destination
mv -n source destination

cases.purpose: With the runner's /dev/null stdin, check that -i declines an overwrite at EOF and compare GNU mv's status, prompt presence, and resulting tree.
cases.script:
printf 'source bytes\n' > source
printf 'destination bytes\n' > destination
mv -i source destination

cases.purpose: Move a symlink without following it and preserve its relative target while leaving the referent unchanged; GNU mv is the independent oracle.
cases.script:
printf 'referent bytes\n' > referent
ln -s referent link
mv link moved-link

cases.purpose: Moving a file onto itself must fail with a diagnostic and preserve the file contents, matching GNU mv.
cases.script:
printf 'preserve me\n' > same
mv same same

cases.purpose: -T forces the destination to be treated as one path; a regular source must not be moved inside an existing directory, matching GNU mv's error and unchanged tree.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf 'source\n' > source
mv -T source destination

cases.purpose: A missing source must fail with a diagnostic and leave the fixture tree unchanged, matching GNU mv.
cases.script: mv missing destination

cases.purpose: Exercise the cross-device fallback for regular files, symlinks, and directory trees while comparing GNU mv and preserving source metadata.
cases.reason: Requires two distinct writable filesystems mounted inside a disposable VM fixture root, or a reviewed syscall mock that makes rename return EXDEV. The provided isolated runner exposes only one writable fixture tree; no mount or host path is used here.

cases.purpose: Bounded here-strings exercise affirmative and negative prompt responses without a PTY.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
if mv -i source target <<< n; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
if mv -i source target <<< y; then b=0; else b=$?; fi
printf '%s %s\n' "$a" "$b"

cases.purpose: Moving between two hardlinks to the same inode must fail and preserve both names.
cases.script:
printf keep > source
ln source alias
mv source alias

cases.purpose: A regular move replaces the destination symlink and leaves its referent and hardlink unchanged.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
ln target hard
ln -s target alias
mv source alias

cases.purpose: A missing middle operand must not prevent later operands from moving.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf first > first
printf last > last
mv first absent last destination

cases.purpose: An EOF refusal should set failure while a later non-colliding source is still moved.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf new > first
printf old > destination/first
printf last > last
mv -i first last destination

cases.purpose: Check existing last -f/-i/-n wins precedence and skipped symlink destinations.
cases.script:
printf a > a
printf b > b
printf c > c
printf old > target
ln -s target alias
mv -fn a alias
mv -nf b target
if mv -ni c target; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf '%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: No-clobber skips existing destinations only for valid sources; a missing source still fails and later operands continue.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf old > destination/absent
printf last > last
mv -n absent last destination

cases.purpose: GNU long options and unambiguous prefixes (guest pass 5, G74): --force, --forc, --interactive, --verbose, options after operands and the -- end of options.
cases.script:
printf a > a; printf b > b; printf c > c; printf d > d
mv --force a b
mv --forc c b
mv --verb d --no-target-directory e
mkdir dir; printf f > -f
mv -- -f dir
printf g > g; mv g -v dir

cases.purpose: Ambiguous, unknown and argument-misuse options are diagnosed with getopt_long's text and coreutils' --help hint, status 1; diagnostics are folded into stdout without the shell prefix.
cases.script:
printf a > a; printf b > b
{ mv --no-c a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv --zzz a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv -z a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv --force=1 a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv a --suffix || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv --update=bogus a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv --backup=bogus a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'

cases.purpose: -b, --backup=CONTROL (with abbreviations), -S/--suffix in both argument forms, and -v naming the backup (G78 mv -b).
cases.script:
printf old > t; printf new > s; mv -b s t
printf 1 > s; mv -v --backup=numbered s t
printf 2 > s; mv -v --backup=t s t
printf 3 > s; mv -v --backup=exist s t
printf 4 > s; mv -v -S .bak s t
printf 5 > s; mv -v --suffix .old s t
printf 6 > s; mv -vb --suff=.x s t
printf 7 > s; VERSION_CONTROL=numbered mv -vb s t
printf 8 > s; mv -v --backup=none s t
cat t; echo

cases.purpose: --backup cannot be combined with -n or --update=none-fail; nothing is moved.
cases.script:
printf old > t; printf new > s
{ mv -bn s t || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv -b --update=none-fail s t || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
cat s t; echo

cases.purpose: -u and --update=all|none|none-fail|older (abbreviated too) decide which existing destinations are replaced.
cases.script:
printf new > s; printf old > t; touch -t 200101010000 t
mv -u s t; cat t; echo
printf newer > s; touch -t 200001010000 s
mv -u s t; cat t; echo
mv --update=none s t; cat t; echo
{ mv --update=none-fail s t || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
mv --upd=al s t; cat t; echo
printf x > s; mv --update s t; cat t

cases.purpose: Missing operands, an extra -T operand, a non-directory target and --strip-trailing-slashes use GNU's text and status 1.
cases.script:
{ mv || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
printf a > a
{ mv a || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
printf b > b; printf c > c
{ mv -T a b c || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv a b c || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv -t c a || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
{ mv -t d -T a || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^.*\(mv\|cp\): /\1: /'
mkdir dir; mv --strip-trailing-slashes dir/ moved

cases.purpose: --exchange swaps two names atomically and reports it with -v.
cases.script:
printf x > a; printf y > b
mv -v --exchange a b
cat a b

cases.purpose: A FIFO moved between the private /tmp tmpfs and the fixture tree is recreated as a FIFO with its mode (rename reports EXDEV), as GNU mv does; -v reports the copy and the removal.
cases.script:
mkfifo -m 640 p
mv p /tmp/p
[ -p /tmp/p ] && [ ! -e p ] && echo moved-out
mv -v /tmp/p q
[ ! -e /tmp/p ] && echo moved-back

cases.purpose: A cross-device move with -b keeps the replaced destination as its backup and -v names it.
cases.script:
printf old > t
printf new > /tmp/n
mv -bv /tmp/n t
cat t t~

cases.purpose: Numbered backups continue after the highest NAME.~N~ (decimal, no leading zero, any length, other names ignored); 'existing' picks numbered only when one exists; -S/SIMPLE_BACKUP_SUFFIX precedence and the '~' fallback for an empty suffix or one with an inner '/'.
cases.script:
mkdir w; cd w
n() { echo *; rm -f ./*; }
touch f s f.~1~ f.~12~; mv --backup=numbered s f; n
touch f s f.~1~ f.~12~; mv --backup=existing s f; n
touch f s; mv --backup=existing s f; n
touch f s f.~01~ f.~0~ f.~1x~ f.~-2~; mv --backup=nil s f; n
touch f s f.~9~; mv --backup=t s f; n
touch f s f.~99999999999999999999~; mv --backup=t s f; n
touch f s ff.~3~ f.~3~~; mv --backup=t s f; n
touch f s; mv -b -S '' s f; n
touch f s; SIMPLE_BACKUP_SUFFIX=.bk mv -b s f; n
touch f s; SIMPLE_BACKUP_SUFFIX=.bk mv -b -S .o s f; n
touch f s; SIMPLE_BACKUP_SUFFIX=.bk mv -b -S a/b s f; n
touch f s; SIMPLE_BACKUP_SUFFIX=/x mv -b s f; n
touch f s; mv -b -S . s f; n
touch f s; { mv -b -S 'a//' s f || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; n
touch f s; VERSION_CONTROL=t mv -b s f; n
touch f s; VERSION_CONTROL=t mv --backup=simple s f; n
touch f s; mv --backup=numbered -b s f; n
touch f s; mv --backup=simple --backup s f; n
mkdir d; touch s d/f d/f.~4~; mv -v --backup=t s d/f; echo d/*

cases.purpose: Invalid and ambiguous --backup and $VERSION_CONTROL values list the valid arguments (synonyms on one line) with the help hint; unambiguous prefixes work; -b conflicts with -n, --update=none(-fail) and --exchange unless a later -f wins; a SOURCE DEST rename into a free name happens before the checks.
cases.script:
for v in n nu bogus "x'y"; do touch a b; { mv --backup="$v" a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; done
touch a b; { VERSION_CONTROL=x mv -b a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch a b; { VERSION_CONTROL=n mv -b a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch a b; VERSION_CONTROL= mv -b a b; VERSION_CONTROL=numbered mv --backup= b a
touch a b; { mv --backup=bogus --backup=numbered a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
for o in -bn '-b --update=none' '-b --update=none-fail' '-b --exchange' '-n -b -f' '-b --update=none-fail --update=all' '-n --backup=bogus'; do
  touch a b; { mv $o a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
done
touch a; { mv -v --backup=bogus a fresh || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch a; { mv -v -bn a fresh2 || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch a; mkdir D; { mv -v -T --backup=bogus a D/x || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
echo *

cases.purpose: The last of -f/-i/-n decides; -n overrides every --update value, --update=none skips silently and none-fail reports 'not replacing', -u and --update follow the last given; checks run before the same-file test only for -n and --update=none(-fail).
cases.script:
touch -d '2030-01-01 00:00' c2
for o in '-u --update=all' '--update=all -u' '-u --update=none' '-n --update=all' '-n -f' '-n -i' '-i -n' '-n --update=older' '--update=none-fail -n' '-f --update=none-fail' '--update=none-fail -i' '--update=none -i' '--upd=al -u' '-u --upd=o'; do
  touch c; { mv $o c c2 || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; [ -e c ] && echo "$o: kept" || echo "$o: moved"; touch -d '2030-01-01 00:00' c2
done
touch a; ln a h
for o in -n --update=none-fail -u -i ''; do { mv $o a h || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; done
touch -d '2000-01-01 00:00' s; mkdir -p F/s; mv -u s F; echo F/*
mkdir -p S1 D1/S1; touch -d '2000-01-01 00:00' S1; mv -uv S1 D1

cases.purpose: -i prompts go to stderr without flushing -v output (GNU's buffered stdout); a declined prompt fails; a just-created destination is never replaced by a later operand (a just-created empty directory may be); an unwritable destination prompts with its mode.
cases.script:
mkdir A B C S; touch A/f B/f C/f S/f
printf 'y\ny\ny\n' | { mv -iv A/f B/f C/f S || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch A/f B/f; printf 'n\ny\n' | { mv -iv A/f B/f S || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
mkdir -p A/d B/d T; { mv -v A/d B/d T || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch A/g B/g; { mv -bv A/g B/g T || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch a b; chmod 444 b; { mv -i a b < /dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; echo
chmod 6555 b; { mv -i a b < /dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; echo
chmod 1444 b; echo y | { mv -iv a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
printf 'yes\nno\n' > ans; touch q r; { mv -i q r; cat; } < ans 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'

cases.purpose: GNU's texts for replacing a directory with a non-directory and back, a non-empty directory, moving a directory into itself, a symlink onto its own target, an unstatable destination and an empty DEST; -b replaces a directory or a hard link by backing it up.
cases.script:
mkdir -p F/a E G/E H; touch a G/E/y F2 f
{ mv a F || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv -i a F < /dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; echo
{ mv H F2 || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv E G || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv H H/sub || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv H H || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv -T H H/ || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv f f/x || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv f '' || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv a ./a || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv -b a ./a || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
ln -s a s; { mv s a || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
mv -bv s a; echo *
ln f h; mv -bv f h
mv -vb F2 F/a; echo F/*
mkdir D; ln -s D L; { mv -T D L || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch t1; ln -s t1 l1; ln -s t1 l2; mv -v l1 l2

cases.purpose: A tree moved to the private /tmp tmpfs and back (rename reports EXDEV) keeps directories, modes (set-group-ID too), hard links, a symlink and a FIFO; -v lists directories created, files copied in inode order (new links to an already copied file are silent) and the sources removed in directory order.
cases.script:
mkdir -p x/y/z; printf 1 > x/y/z/f; ln x/y/z/f x/l; ln -s ../f x/y/s; mkfifo -m 640 x/p; chmod 2750 x/y; chmod 604 x/y/z/f
mv -v x /tmp/x
[ -p /tmp/x/p ] && [ ! -e x ] && echo moved-out
mv -v /tmp/x back
[ ! -e /tmp/x ] && [ -p back/p ] && cat back/l back/y/z/f && echo
printf 1 > a; ln a b; mv -v a b /tmp/; mv -v /tmp/a /tmp/b .

cases.purpose: Across file systems: an unreadable source fails with GNU's message, leaves no partial file and puts the -b backup back ('(unbackup)'); a directory with an unreadable member is copied as far as possible and nothing is removed; --no-copy refuses; -u skips a newer destination; a non-empty destination directory is not replaced; --debug adds the copy report.
cases.script:
trap 'chmod 600 u T/u 2>/dev/null || :' EXIT
printf u > u; chmod 0 u; printf old > /tmp/u
{ mv -bv u /tmp/ || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
cat /tmp/u; echo; [ -e /tmp/u~ ] || echo no-backup-left
mkdir T; printf a > T/a; printf u > T/u; chmod 0 T/u; printf z > T/z
{ mv -v T /tmp/ || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
cat T/a T/z /tmp/T/a /tmp/T/z; echo; [ -e /tmp/T/u ] || echo no-partial-u
chmod 600 u T/u
printf n > n; { mv --no-copy n /tmp/n || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
touch -d '2030-01-01 00:00' /tmp/n; mv -vu n /tmp/n; [ -e n ] && echo kept-older
mkdir -p U /tmp/U/q; printf a > U/a; { mv -v U /tmp/ || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
mkdir -p V /tmp/V; printf a > V/a; mv -v V /tmp/
printf d > dbg; mv --debug dbg /tmp/dbg; mv --debug /tmp/dbg dbg2; mv --debug dbg2 dbg3

cases.purpose: --exchange needs an existing destination (GNU prints 'Unknown error -1'), refuses the same file, honours -n/-i/--update and exchanges a directory with a file under -T; --strip-trailing-slashes keeps a non-directory SOURCE from being renamed to a name of its own, and target directories with trailing slashes get none doubled.
cases.script:
touch a; { mv -v --exchange a nofile || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
mkdir D; { mv -v --exchange a D || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
ln a h; { mv --exchange a h || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
printf 1 > a; printf 2 > b; mv --exchange -n a b; { mv --exchange -i a b < /dev/null || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; echo
{ mv --exchange --update=none-fail a b || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'; cat a b; echo
mv -v -T --exchange D a; [ -d a ] && [ -f D ] && echo swapped
touch f g; mkdir Q E; { mv -v --strip-trailing-slashes f/ Q || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
{ mv -v --strip-trailing-slashes g/ new || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
mkdir R; mv -v --strip-trailing-slashes R/// R2
{ mv -v g/ x || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed -E 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //g'
mv -v g E//; mv -v -t E// Q; mv -v E//g .//
